title: Dark Chocolate Raspberry Tart
description: A crisp chocolate pastry shell filled with silky dark chocolate ganache and crowned with a ring of raspberries.

ingredients.name: egg yolk
ingredients.note: plus 1–2 tbsp cold water if needed

steps.text: Make the pastry: blitz the flour, cocoa, icing sugar and salt in a food processor, then pulse in the butter until the mixture looks like coarse sand.
Add the yolk and pulse, adding cold water a spoonful at a time, until the dough just comes together. Shape into a disc, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out and line a 24 cm fluted tart tin with a removable base. Trim the edges and chill again for 20 minutes.
Line the shell with baking paper and baking beans and blind-bake at 180°C fan for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and bake 8–10 minutes more until dry and crisp. Cool completely.
Make the ganache: heat the cream, sugar and vanilla in a small pan until steaming (do not boil). Pour over the chopped chocolate, stand for 2 minutes, then stir slowly until smooth and glossy.
Pour the ganache into the cooled shell and gently level the surface.
Chill for 3 hours until set, then arrange the raspberries in rings over the top and scatter with the pistachios. Serve cold.

notesMarkdown:
## Blind baking

A crisp, **fully baked** shell is non-negotiable — under-baked chocolate pastry goes
soggy the moment the ganache lands. If the edges colour early, cover them with foil.

## Substitutions

- **Raspberries:** sliced strawberries or a quenelle of clotted cream instead.
- **Chocolate:** milk chocolate makes a softer, sweeter ganache — reduce the sugar to 1 tbsp.

## Storage & freezing

Keeps 2 days in the fridge, covered. The finished tart freezes well (without the
berries) for up to a month; add the fruit after thawing.
